$comment: Terrain volumes (docs/proposals/TERRAIN_HYDROLOGY_AND_VOLUMES.md §3 layer 2; ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3): a 3D density per cell over the height field, solid where it is above 0. A volume's `density` is a tree of nodes from a fixed vocabulary: a number (a constant); "depth" (m from the cell's centre down from the height field's surface: > 0 below it); "height" (m above sea level); {"slope": {"radius"}} (the surface's gradient over ±radius m, rise per run); {"noise": {"wavelength", "octaves", "stretchY", "stream"}} (3D gradient noise in [-1, 1], its vertical frequency stretchY times the horizontal one, 0 a 2D field); {"add" | "mul" | "min" | "max": [nodes]}; {"abs": node}; {"clamp": {"of", "min", "max"}}; {"smoothstep": {"of", "from", "to"}}. Only cells within `reach` m of the surface are evaluated; beyond it the height field stands. The reshaped ground's topmost solid cell is each column's top (docs/WORLD_GENERATION.md §5): the ground is filled, ramped, decorated and planted from it as from the height field, with at most `soilDepth` m of soil under a top (never less than the terrain's `underDepth`; so a cliff face shows rock); the cells the density removes under it become air, or water under the column's own water; a floor left under rock is the top block where open sky lies within `floorGrass` m of it, else `material`, as is a ceiling. The prototype world type `cliffs` (generator 101) uses the volume named "cliffs"; the LOD draws the height field's top surface only.

volumes.name: cliffs
volumes.$comment: Cliffs and overhangs: in the part of the land a 600 m field picks (listed first: a product stops at a zero factor, so the slope is measured only there), on hillsides (slope 0.3 to 0.8 over ±4 m), a thresholded 3D noise (40 m across, ~27 m tall) lifts the ground 14 m or sinks it 14 m with a sharp edge between: rock walls with ledges on top, leaning where the edge leans (overhangs).
